why: the opaque module identity and the heap core's transition key cover the code the unit reaches (langs/ts/reach.mjs, design/hash-keys.md), each case is check.mjs on a parent and its candidate. (1) three regress units on their real files: an edit elsewhere in the file (a comment and another function; a constructor's parameter type) leaves them PASS-proved. (2) a sibling the unit does not reach changes: hasTag (an opaque module unit reading a module regex; normalize, shout and a comment change) and cost (an outside call; Tally.add and scale change) are PASS-proved. (3) a sibling the unit reaches changes behaviour: hasMention (normalize), hasCode (the module regex it reads), priced (scale) are WITNESS; enroll hands a Tally to the outside, whose add changed: lane A does not prove it (the transition's key carries Tally's code) and lane B's fake never runs add, so PASS-bounded, never PASS-proved. (4) through a class member and a base-class member: Cart.charge reads a field and calls outside while Cart.rate and Cart.note change (PASS-proved), Cart.fee calls the changed this.rate (WITNESS); Parser.strict reads a module regex while the base class Base.norm and Base.label and the sibling Parser.name change (PASS-proved), Parser.loose calls the inherited, changed this.norm (WITNESS), Parser.name changed itself (WITNESS).
